So far it certainly seems like instead of being populated mostly by left-wing extremists we have right-wing extremists. Everyone is terrified of the not-that-threatening SJW threat. I've seen a small handful of people genuinely afraid of political correctness and just generally being nice to each other. Honestly, it seems to be an alternative reddit inhabited by what I remember of the 4chan community. Right now, it's the /r/atheism of reddit, and it's a little bit silly. Hopefully it will go in a different direction.

At any rate, it is very refreshing to see people who are able to disagree with each other without using the word circlejerk. On reddit, it was as if two people couldn't agree with each other without cries of circlejerking being taken seriously.

The less politicized boards (e.g. /v/aww, /v/movies) seem to have the content you'd expect and merely have smaller communities. As voat grows, these communities will as well, and that's something I look forward to.

In regards to the threats of corruption and admin abuse, it does appear that there are efforts in the very coding of the site that will help to lessen the power that moderators and administrators can wield. For example, comments that have been removed by a moderator are marked as such, instead of leaving only the [deleted] text, which could also be produced when a user deleted his or her own comment. I've not been here long enough to be familiar with any others, but I'm sure they're there. Additionally, since you must obtain a number of contribution points in a subverse to downvote, the "downvote brigades" that you might sometimes encounter on reddit would be far less impactful here.
Unfortunately, how a community turns out isn't always necessarily decided. It's something that just happens over time. We just need to cycle through mods so they don't get power trips or something.

Go to reddit and start a thread to discuss the ongoing legal issues of reddit CEO Ellen Pao and her husband Alphonse "Buddy" Fletcher. If it makes it to the front page, as many have, it gets nuked. Check out /v/MeanwhileOnReddit for various examples of other things being censored on the site. Like others have said the signal:noise ratio is pretty bad on Reddit, but the thing that finally pushed me away was the rapidly increasing amount of censorship. Ultimately I think a major problem is something I just posted about - Reddit is part of a multibillion dollar mass media company . That leads to a major conflict of interest when it comes to discussing a variety of topics. Ellen and Buddy's legal troubles have created a scenario that provided a perfect direct litmus test to see how committed Reddit is to free speech when that free speech may negatively effect the company. And they've failed spectacularly.

So how is this community going to be different? Like others have mentioned the developers are integrating technical means to ensure some degree of accountability persists. In today's world where people seem to be treating getting offended at the most inane things as a badge of honor, I don't like engaging in a forum where I have to worry about a conversation getting silently and overtly censored because somebody opposes it decided to get "offended" by it.
By not invalidating an entire comment because of a single spelling or grammar mistake. I have tried to have discussions on Reddit and because of a single mistype my entire argument was thrown out.

I would love to see the community come together as an actual community where content creators within the community receive support and discussions are treated as opportunities to find new ideas and not just disagree. These are the two things that Reddit has failed at the most. Especially the content created by members, it is seen as self promotion and not an offering to community. YouTube supports internal content creators, soundcloud supports content creators, and if voat wants to really take hold we must support our content creators as well.

A big step in supporting the content creators is by discussing things as a means to finding new ideas, not just a hivemind circle jerk of ideas. But that all requires a bit of maturity and self awareness. I don't know if people on the internet can put away their Id enough for that.
